title: An `IHDR` declaring a compression method the specification does not define
why: `IHDR` carries a compression method and a filter method, and the specification defines exactly one of each. Ignoring those two bytes means inflating ordinary-looking scanlines and reaching a *gate verdict* where a conforming decoder reaches `decode-failed` — the same class as an interlaced file, and the same token. The method byte is written *into* the chunk, so its CRC is correct: poking it into a finished file would leave a stale CRC, and the file would then be refused by the CRC check before the method byte was ever read — a fixture that passes for the wrong reason.
